## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/01_hook.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
The most-searched AI job title in America right now is one almost nobody was tracking.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/02_reveal.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Forward deployed engineer.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/03_palantir.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Palantir coined it over a decade ago - an engineer embedded with the customer. It stayed a Palantir word for about ten years.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/04_forty_x.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Then it went up about forty times in eighteen months.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/05_method.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Four years of US Google search volume, every AI job title I could assemble.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/06_honest_signal.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Nobody types a job title into Google to look good. It is one of the few honest signals we have.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/07_four_lines.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Four titles carry the whole chart.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/08_fde.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Forward deployed engineer went from an in-joke to the top of the list.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/09_prompt_engineer.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Prompt engineer, the first title to break out after ChatGPT, peaked in spring 2023 and has slid ever since.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/10_karpathy.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
Context engineer was flat for almost three years. Then Karpathy posted this.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/11_context_engineer.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
The line turns in the same weeks - then gives most of it back. Excellent post. Weak job title.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/12_ai_engineer.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
AI engineer just climbs. No spike, no collapse. The dullest line on the chart, and the one I trust most.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/13_duration.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
The difference is duration. Spread through hiring, a title climbs for months and holds. Spread through a post, it climbs for weeks and gives it back.
:::

## {background-image="output_v2/slides_video/14_kicker.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#FAF8F5"}

::: {.notes}
And standing inside the spike, the two look identical.
:::
